chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father. He said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both) when a man from the Khawarij came to him and said: O Abu Ja'far, what thing do you worship? He said: Allah. He said: Did you see Him? He said: The eyes have not seen Him through direct observation, but the hearts have seen Him through the realities of faith. He is not known by analogy, nor is He compared to people. He is described by His signs and known by His indicators. He does not oppress in His judgment. That is Allah, there is no deity except Him.
He said: So the man left while saying: Allah is most knowing of where He places His message.

key_terms.الْخَوَارِج: The Khawarij (Kharijites), an early Islamic sect known for their extreme literalism and opposition to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الْعِيَان: Direct visual observation; the Imam contrasts physical sight with spiritual perception through faith
key_terms.الْقِيَاس: Analogy or comparison; a method of reasoning rejected when applied to knowing God's nature

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about seeing God when a Kharijite questioned him?
ai.summary: This hadith records a dialogue between Imam al-Baqir (AS) and a Kharijite who challenged him about worshipping what cannot be seen. The Imam's response articulates the classical Shia theological position on divine transcendence: God cannot be perceived by physical sight or understood through human analogy, but is known through the heart's faith and through His signs in creation. The Kharijite was so impressed that he departed affirming Quranic verse 6:124 about God's wisdom in choosing His messengers.
